subtitle: Families and communities take many forms. Understand chosen relationships and learned meanings, without assuming who speaks or decides for someone.
scope: For staff across DHS. Original personal and community examples compare meanings of family, belonging, responsibility and chosen support. They are not national profiles, legal definitions of family, capacity findings or instructions about an actual authorized representative. Participation in this learning is voluntary. Actual agency responsibilities, access requirements and decision authority remain. Native American- and Tribal-specific matters are referred to the appropriate office within ADSA.
introTranscript: Family and community can mean connection, history, responsibility, chosen support or something else to a particular person. Similar words can carry different meanings, and people within a relationship can disagree. Explore what is actually wanted, understand your own first interpretation and choose a response that preserves personal agency and the relationships the person values.

intro.heading: Begin with what the relationship means here
intro.body:
Family and community are meaningful words, but they do not tell you everything about a particular relationship. Someone may value a relative’s memories, a friend’s advice, a neighborhood connection or the ability to decide privately. The significance can come from learned practices and lived experience. It cannot be supplied merely by a surname, household arrangement or assumed group identity.

The example concerns a neighborhood photo event. Maia is considering contributing a picture of a street celebration. Maia asks grandmother Dara to help remember when the picture was taken and friend Ivo to help compare two possible captions. The event organizer, Soren, assumes that involving Dara means the family will choose what Maia contributes. The supplied request establishes help with a date, not that authority or a complete decision-making arrangement.

Maia also says that a personal note in the picture’s envelope should not appear publicly. This is a current content preference. The example does not establish a legal records rule, ownership of every item or authority to reproduce someone else’s photograph. The organizer still needs the actual event permissions and arrangements before displaying material. Respecting Maia’s account includes keeping these different questions clear.

The Council of Europe source explains that people participate in multiple cultures, including families and other groups, and use those resources in personalized ways. That supports an inquiry about what this relationship means to Maia. It does not supply a universal family structure or make Dara responsible for representing everyone with a similar background. Different people in the same family may attach different meanings to the same exchange.

A useful beginning is therefore specific: “What would you like Dara and Ivo to help with, and what would you like to keep private?” Maia may describe a purpose, change the request or decline a personal explanation. The relevant answer concerns the contribution now being considered. No one needs to reveal an entire family history to be taken seriously.

For private practice, compare Maia’s two actual requests with Soren’s larger assumption. You may also notice a comfortable relationship meaning of your own and keep it unrecorded. Understanding your first interpretation can be worthwhile before a photograph is displayed or any workplace process changes. You can use the example; do not enter sensitive information about another person.

items.title: The purpose is more precise than the label
items.body: Dara is a grandmother and is asked to help recall the date. That specific purpose matters more than a prediction about family authority. If Soren treats the label as the whole account, Maia’s wanted help could become a decision transfer nobody requested.

items.title: Different help can coexist
items.body: Ivo helps compare captions while Dara contributes a memory. Maia need not choose one relationship as the only legitimate source of support. Keeping the purposes distinct allows useful participation without assuming that both helpers receive every item or decide the final contribution.

items.title: Content choice and actual permission differ
items.body: Maia’s preference keeps the personal note out of the proposed public display. The event’s actual permissions still need examination for the photograph and caption. A chosen support conversation does not grant reproduction rights or prove that every person shown has agreed.

tabs.label: Clarify wanted involvement
tabs.body: Ask the purpose and scope of Dara’s and Ivo’s help, then retain Maia’s opportunity to express a choice. This responds to the actual request instead of guessing from relationship labels. It can also make the remaining permission and privacy questions easier to address.

tabs.label: Assign family authority
tabs.body: Letting Dara make the final choice because she is a grandmother adds a power not supplied in the example. It could turn valued advice into a gate for Maia’s participation. A relationship may matter deeply without establishing legal or event decision authority.

tabs.label: Exclude all help
tabs.body: Demanding that Maia prepare everything alone would remove wanted assistance to prove a particular model of independence. That is also an assumption. The example supports clarifying the help, not deciding that personal agency requires solitude or that advice automatically replaces choice.

check.question: What does Maia’s request establish?
check.correct: Dara is asked to help recall the date and Ivo to compare captions; wider authority and permissions are not established by those requests.
wrong: Dara must choose the contribution because she is a grandmother.
Ivo may publish the personal note because help was requested.
Maia must work alone for the choice to be genuine.
check.feedbackCorrect: This retains the supplied purpose of each relationship while leaving authority and content permissions distinct.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A family label does not establish decision authority. Requested help does not permit publishing the private note. Working alone is not the only way to own a choice. Each alternative replaces Maia’s specific account with an unsupported relationship rule.

intro.heading: Compare meanings of care and responsible choice
intro.body:
The story now supplies learned meanings rather than leaving Soren to predict them. Dara learned through a neighborhood growing circle that comparing ideas before planting showed responsibility for shared consequences. In that experience, giving an idea was care, not a demand that the other person accept it. Dara wants to help Maia remember the date and says Maia should decide what to contribute.

Ivo learned through a youth reading group that responding to a person’s own first interpretation showed trust in their voice. Ivo initially waits for Maia’s preferred caption before commenting. Maia reads the delay as a reluctance to help, while Ivo reads Dara’s early suggestion as pressure. These first interpretations are understandable but incomplete. Each person is applying a learned meaning to someone else’s behavior.

After hearing the accounts, Maia says that an early date suggestion is useful and that comparing the two captions together is wanted. Maia would like to hear Ivo’s view without first choosing a final answer. Dara and Ivo can adapt: identify which date remains uncertain, discuss the captions as options, and ask what Maia wants to use. The response changes because the particular meanings and current request were understood.

This is not a contest between a collective family and an independent friend. The official Hofstede page specifically cautions that collectivism is not simply closeness. Its national-level descriptions do not classify Dara, Ivo or Maia. Their supplied practices arise from particular growing and reading groups, and each may use other practices elsewhere. Describing every family exchange with a broad category would conceal the distinctions the example actually provides.

Neither account controls the event’s factual and permission questions. A remembered date remains a recollection to check as appropriate, and a helpful caption suggestion is not permission to reproduce material. Maia’s wanted consultation does not automatically authorize someone else to speak publicly about the private note. Meaningful help and actual boundaries can be examined together.

Privately consider whether you equate unsolicited advice with pressure or waiting with indifference. You may use the example rather than a real relationship. Recognizing another plausible meaning can deepen self-understanding without requiring you to adopt every practice or produce an event contribution. The person’s present choice still matters.

items.title: Early advice can mean care
items.body: Dara’s growing-circle account explains why comparing ideas early can express responsibility. That is evidence of the meaning Dara supplies, not proof that all advice is welcome. Maia’s present request determines whether the suggestion fits this conversation, and disagreement remains possible.

items.title: Waiting can mean trust
items.body: Ivo’s reading-group account explains a wish not to replace another person’s voice. Hearing Maia’s request lets Ivo offer a comparison without treating silence as the only respectful method. The adapted response preserves the purpose of trust while changing how it is communicated.

items.title: The new conversation follows the accounts
items.body: Dara clarifies uncertainty and Ivo compares the captions while Maia retains a choice. That is a particular response to particular meanings. Merely renaming the people collective or independent would not explain how the conversation changed or what remains unresolved.

tabs.label: Advice with agency
tabs.body: Offer the requested recollection and caption comparison, identify uncertainty and ask Maia’s preference. This follows the accounts of care and trust without requiring acceptance. Wanted advice can support a person’s own direction when its purpose and limits are clear.

tabs.label: Advice as an obligation
tabs.body: Demanding that Maia accept Dara’s suggestion as gratitude would turn the account of care into a rule Dara did not supply. It could make the relationship a gate to participation. A valued contribution does not require agreement with every suggestion.

tabs.label: Silence as the only respect
tabs.body: Ivo’s waiting has an understandable purpose, but Maia now asks for a comparison. Refusing to respond until Maia decides would preserve a method while missing its intended meaning. Adaptation can retain trust in the person’s voice while changing the timing of help.

Assign the three people permanent national cultural profiles.
check.feedbackCorrect: The response links learned care and trust to the requested help without turning either meaning into a personal rank or authority.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Gratitude does not require agreement. Waiting is not the only respectful method once a comparison is wanted. The supplied accounts do not establish national profiles. These shortcuts substitute a rule for the particular meanings and current request.

lessons.statement: Make room for individual accounts without making one person the whole community.

intro.heading: Hear differences within a family or community
intro.body:
Comparative learning becomes more useful when it recognizes variation within the categories it compares. A family, club or neighborhood can contain different memories, roles and wishes. Some practices are shared, others are contested, and a person can draw on several affiliations at once. Hearing one account should not turn it into a complete community voice.

In the example, a neighbor asks Dara to provide the one family view of the street celebration. Dara remembers the planting-group contribution and values naming who brought food. Another relative, Len, values the chance to meet new neighbors and remembers the music most clearly. Maia is interested in how the picture shows participation across different ages. These accounts concern the same event without being interchangeable or mutually invalid.

A suitable invitation allows each wanted contribution to keep its scope. Maia can use Dara’s remembered date as a recollection to check, consider Len’s account when wanted and choose what belongs in the caption under the event’s actual permissions. Dara should not be made responsible for answering every question about the family. Nor should Len’s different memory be treated as disloyalty or proof that no shared experience occurred.

A separate private fiction concerns Willa. In a family singing circle, Willa learned that joining a familiar song could express belonging without much explanation. In a later volunteer group, explicitly choosing which task to take conveyed reliable participation. Willa recognizes a first interpretation that saying no to one song means rejecting the family. Considering the second meaning makes room for belonging alongside personal choice.

You may examine a comfortable value, affiliation or memory in private, or use Willa’s fiction. The insight can remain meaningful even if no family discussion follows and no shared agreement is reached. Do not demand a painful history, publish someone else’s private account or make consensus the test of legitimate self-understanding.

This learning also keeps important distinctions. Multiple viewpoints do not mean every factual claim is equally supported, and recognizing a relationship does not establish legal authority to consent for someone else. The sources’ emphasis on personalized meanings supports careful listening, not a rule that every version must be printed or every disagreement ignored.

lessons.keyStatement: Make room for individual accounts without making one person the whole community.

items.title: A particular voice is still useful
items.body: Dara’s recollection can illuminate one part of the celebration without representing every relative. Naming that scope preserves its value and makes appropriate checking possible. Demanding the single family account would add a role Dara did not accept and could hide other wanted perspectives.

items.title: Difference does not erase relationship
items.body: Len’s interest in music and Maia’s interest in participation can coexist with Dara’s contribution memory. A different emphasis is not evidence of disloyalty or lack of belonging. The actual caption question can consider relevant accounts without forcing one identical meaning.

items.title: Private reflection need not produce consensus
items.body: Willa can reconsider the meaning of declining a song without asking the whole family to agree. Understanding a learned association is a legitimate personal outcome. The example avoids disclosure pressure and leaves any later conversation genuinely optional.

tabs.label: Particular accounts
tabs.body: Identify who supplied each memory and what it addresses. This lets Maia compare relevant contributions without declaring one person the family representative. The caption still needs actual factual and permission checks; recognizing different meanings does not settle those questions.

tabs.label: One representative answer
tabs.body: Asking Dara for the official family meaning would make a personal contribution carry more than it establishes. Other perspectives could disappear behind a familiar relationship label. A person may offer a useful account without speaking for every relative or neighbor.

tabs.label: No shared value possible
tabs.body: Treating variation as proof that family or community connection is meaningless makes the opposite overclaim. People can share a relationship while valuing different parts of it. Willa’s private learning can likewise preserve belonging and choice without total agreement.

check.feedbackCorrect: This preserves useful variation and legitimate personal understanding without an invented representative role.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The grandmother role does not supply everyone’s view. A different memory does not prove disloyalty. Private insight does not require public consensus. Each alternative makes belonging depend on a rule the supplied accounts do not establish.

lessons.statement: Keep the meaning of giving separate from the obligation someone actually accepted.

intro.heading: Distinguish reciprocity from a compulsory obligation
intro.body:
Reciprocity can involve giving and receiving that sustain a relationship, but its meaning should be understood in the particular account. It is not a universal exchange rate or a reason to require gratitude performances. People may value a contribution deeply while choosing differently from the advice offered.

In the example, Dara explains that bringing a remembered detail to the photo event recalls a neighborhood practice of contributing something rather than only receiving hospitality. Maia values that help and thanks Dara, then chooses the other caption suggested in the conversation. Dara says this is acceptable: the recollection was an offered contribution, not a condition that Maia use a particular caption. The account demonstrates care without required agreement.

Soren then assumes Ivo will collect and scan all the family photographs because Ivo is a friend and has already helped. That is a separate unsupported commitment. Ivo agreed to compare two captions, not to manage an archive or receive the envelope’s private note. The wanted relationship does not create unlimited work, access or responsibility.

A useful response names the actual offers and asks separately about any new task. Maia and the event organizer can clarify what material is proposed, what remains private, which permissions apply and whether a person voluntarily accepts another contribution. If no one accepts the scanning task, the event needs an honest account of that condition rather than a practice commitment inserted to make the plan appear complete.

This is also a chance to understand your own learned expectations. Perhaps help feels incomplete unless you repay immediately, or refusing a suggestion feels ungrateful even when the giver expects free choice. You can privately compare those possibilities with Dara’s account without declaring any method universally wrong. A comfortable reflection or the example is sufficient; no actual family task or disclosure is required.

Meaning does not remove other responsibilities. Actual ownership, reproduction permissions and any real authorized-representative role need their proper examination; the course decides none of them. It teaches a narrower distinction: a valued relationship and a meaningful contribution do not by themselves establish agreement, access to private material or a new unpaid task.

items.title: The thanks need not decide the caption
items.body: Maia can appreciate Dara’s recollection and choose the other caption. Dara’s account explicitly leaves that choice open. Treating gratitude as acceptance would turn a voluntary contribution into a condition neither person supplied, making care less accurately understood.

items.title: A new task needs a new account
items.body: Ivo’s comparison help does not establish responsibility for scanning all photographs. Clarifying the proposal and any voluntary offer avoids using friendship as an administrative shortcut. An unanswered task can stay unanswered while the event seeks a feasible arrangement.

items.title: Privacy does not reject the relationship
items.body: Keeping the envelope’s note private does not erase the wanted help. The material boundary and the relationship can coexist. Asking Ivo to receive everything as proof of trust would introduce an unwanted demand, not demonstrate the care or contribution described in the example.

tabs.label: A bounded contribution
tabs.body: Describe Dara’s recollection and Ivo’s caption comparison accurately, retaining Maia’s choice and private note. A new task can be proposed separately. This preserves meaningful help without silently expanding who does the work or what information they receive.

tabs.label: Gratitude as compulsory agreement
tabs.body: Requiring Maia to choose Dara’s caption would make appreciation a decision gate. The giver’s actual account does not require that exchange. It could also hide the difference between valuing the contribution and finding a particular suggestion suitable for the picture.

tabs.label: Friendship as unlimited work
tabs.body: Assigning scanning and archive access to Ivo would make relationship warmth substitute for an actual offer. The event might then rely on unavailable help or disclose unwanted material. Confirm scope and practical arrangements rather than treating a friend as a default provider.

check.feedbackCorrect: This keeps the meaningful contribution distinct from a new commitment or disclosure demand.
check.feedbackIncorrect: One accepted task does not establish every later commitment. A private note need not be published to prove trust. Gratitude does not require accepting the caption. These shortcuts use a relationship meaning to impose work, access or agreement not supplied in the case.

lessons.statement: Use relationship understanding to improve inquiry while retaining actual roles and duties.

intro.heading: Carry understanding into DHS without inventing authority
intro.body:
The community fiction does not define legal family status or decide consent for a DHS service. Its useful application is a question staff can carry into actual work: what relationship and participation does the person want, and what responsibilities apply in this setting? Wanted advice, a public contribution, access to records and an actual authorized-representative role are different matters.

In a separate example, a DHS workgroup is reviewing a general public information page. Eli proposes treating one family member’s comments as the complete view of everyone who might use the page. The comments can be useful, but their scope remains one supplied perspective. They do not establish the preferences of every relative, authority to disclose another person’s records or evidence that the page works for all readers.

A more careful approach asks what the contribution actually addresses, which relevant perspectives are missing and how they can be sought appropriately within the workgroup’s actual role and available arrangements. Family and community contributors should not be made unpaid representatives of entire populations or asked for sensitive disclosures to validate a concern. If a real representative or consent role is relevant, use the actual authority and process instead of inferring it from a relationship label.

DHS Equity Policy retains actual staff responsibilities, including use of equity analysis in agency work and applicable actions. This course does not replace a required analysis with an optional conversation or approve a custom decision process. Staff own their work and develop capability; the consultant offers guidance and feedback rather than performing every task or imposing a universal consultation gate. Actual access and program responsibilities remain distinct from the learning exercise.

In another example, manager Nia hears an allegation that an employee was excluded from work opportunities because of perceived national origin. Under MMB Policy 1436, managers and supervisors immediately report protected-class allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow agency procedures. Describing the exclusion as a family or community difference does not settle the allegation or postpone that duty.

The course makes no finding. Actual assigned investigation roles and nonretaliation remain; a learning group cannot demand a cultural explanation or public reconciliation before a required response. For private practice, compare the perspective, authority and duty questions using the example. No actual service records, employee identities or family history need to be entered.

items.title: A useful comment keeps its scope
items.body: The family member’s suggestion can identify a wording question on the public page. It does not represent every reader or establish access for all. Keeping that scope clear preserves the contribution and makes it possible to seek other relevant information without making the person responsible for an entire population.

items.title: Wanted involvement is not every authority
items.body: Someone may want a relative to compare options without authorizing them to receive all records or consent to a service. If an actual representative role matters, its scope needs the proper process. The course cannot resolve it through a family word or a cultural preference.

items.title: The manager’s timing remains immediate
items.body: Nia’s role and the supplied national-origin allegation retain the actual policy response. An optional cultural conversation can support understanding later without delaying reporting. Reporting is not a finding, and agency procedures govern any responsibilities properly assigned in the investigation.

tabs.label: Perspective informs actual work
tabs.body: Use the comment for the question it addresses, identify missing perspectives appropriately and retain actual analysis and decision roles. This invites useful contribution without making one family voice universal. Relationship understanding can improve the inquiry while evidence and authority keep their own scope.

tabs.label: Relationship supplies consent
tabs.body: Allowing a relative to receive records or decide a service solely from a label invents authority. Wanted support may have a narrower purpose. The actual representative, privacy and program processes matter; a classroom relationship comparison does not determine them.

tabs.label: Community explanation closes a report
tabs.body: Attributing an allegation to community differences does not decide whether conduct violated policy or fulfill Nia’s reporting duty. The manager immediately uses the stated path and follows agency procedures. Learning does not require informal reconciliation before that response.

intro.heading: Recognize connection and choice without a universal result
intro.body:
The photo-event fiction ends with Maia choosing a caption after comparing the ideas. The group checks the date as far as the available information allows and marks the remaining uncertainty appropriately. Under the event’s actual arrangements and permissions, the selected picture and caption are displayed. The personal note is not published, and Ivo has not been assigned the wider archive task.

Maia says the conversation preserved the wanted help and the final choice. Dara says the remembered contribution was heard without requiring agreement. Ivo says the request clarified how to offer a view. These are particular supplied accounts, not a measurement of an entire family or community. The event has not collected every visitor’s experience, and a future scanning arrangement remains undecided.

The useful learning is the connection among meaning, choice and actual scope. Dara’s care did not become a gratitude gate. Ivo’s trust did not require permanent silence. Maia’s private note did not have to become public proof of belonging. Actual event permission and the unanswered future task retained their own questions instead of being filled by a relationship assumption.

A final account can recognize this result without declaring that all family relationships are harmonious, every community voice was represented or all advice supports choice. It can also avoid the opposite overclaim that any uncertainty makes the contribution worthless. The present accounts support a specific understanding and response; later experience may add or change information.

Willa’s private recognition remains a valid learning outcome. Belonging can coexist with choosing not to join one activity. Dara’s and Ivo’s accounts may also help you notice a comfortable learned meaning of care or responsibility. No family consensus, public personal history or workplace improvement is required before that understanding matters. You may use the example and leave the reflection unrecorded.

For final practice, describe one learned meaning, the response it informed and one practical or authority question it could not settle. This keeps cultural understanding connected to reality without making a family or community profile. Any DHS application retains actual evidence, access, privacy, roles and responsibilities. Learning can deepen connection and personal agency while remaining honest about what is unknown.

lessons.keyStatement: Recognize the meaningful connection while keeping the claim specific.

items.title: The accounts describe a particular success
items.body: Maia reports wanted help and retained choice, while Dara and Ivo describe the clarified exchange. These accounts can be valued without being generalized to everyone. The future task and visitor experiences remain open, so the final summary should not declare total representation or permanent harmony.

items.title: The practical boundary remains visible
items.body: The note was kept out of the public contribution and the wider scanning task was not assigned by assumption. Those are specific outcomes under the supplied arrangement. They do not certify all permissions, future privacy or service authority beyond the example.

items.title: A private insight needs no family performance
items.body: Willa can understand belonging alongside choice without arranging a public discussion or getting consensus. A learner can use the example rather than personal memories. Self-understanding is legitimate in its own right, alongside optional practical application within an actual role.

tabs.label: A specific final account
tabs.body: Describe the chosen contribution, bounded help and particular responses, retaining the unknown visitor experience and future task. This gives the relationship learning substance without claiming everyone agrees. It can guide a relevant next question while respecting the person’s present choice.

tabs.label: Universal relationship harmony
tabs.body: Declaring that every family concern is resolved would exceed the supplied accounts and could hide a different experience. A positive result for three people is useful but does not establish permanent trust or one community view. Keep its actual scope clear.

tabs.label: No value without disclosure
tabs.body: Requiring Willa or the learner to publish a family memory would make privacy a failure condition. The course allows practice and unrecorded understanding. A public story, group consensus or work measure is not needed to make a thoughtful relationship insight meaningful.

check.question: Which final account fits the example?
check.correct: The contribution preserves Maia’s choice and bounded help, with particular positive accounts while future tasks and other experiences remain open.
wrong: Every relative and visitor now holds the same family meaning.
A future task proves the present contribution failed.
Willa must publish a family memory and obtain agreement before insight matters.
check.feedbackCorrect: This recognizes the specific connection and choice while preserving unknowns and legitimate private learning.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The available accounts cannot establish everyone’s meaning. An open future task does not erase the current contribution. Private self-understanding does not require publication or consensus. The alternatives either overstate the evidence or impose an unwanted learning gate.

jobAid.subtitle: Understand the wanted relationship, preserve personal choice and keep practical authority clear.
remember: A family or community label does not establish one preference, every obligation or an official representative role.
Wanted help can support personal agency without replacing the person’s direction.
A contribution can express care or reciprocity without requiring agreement, gratitude performances or unwanted disclosure.
Private personal or practice self-understanding can remain meaningful without consensus or a workplace result.

sections.heading: Clarify the particular relationship
items: Ask whom the person wants involved, for what purpose and with which information. Keep requested help distinct from authority to decide, receive records or consent.
Listen to individually meanings the people describe of care, trust, contribution and belonging. Different people within the same relationship may have different accounts.
Use the Maia/Dara/Ivo/Willa an example or a comfortable private reflection. Do not make a painful family story or a public cultural explanation a participation requirement.

sections.heading: Preserve choice and actual commitments
items: Offer the wanted comparison or contribution without making acceptance the price of gratitude. Confirm any new task separately rather than assuming unpaid help from kinship or friendship.
Keep the person’s content boundaries alongside actual ownership, permission, privacy and representative processes. A relationship meaning does not settle every legal or practical question.
Describe each contributor’s actual perspective and what it addresses. One voice does not represent an entire family, community or service population.

sections.heading: Apply and review within your role
items: Retain actual DHS equity-analysis requirements, evidence and decision responsibilities. Optional consultant guidance supports staff capability rather than replacing staff work or imposing a universal gate.

Managers and supervisors immediately report protected-class harassment or discrimination allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer under MMB Policy 1436 and follow agency procedures. Learning and informal reconciliation do not delay reporting or replace assigned investigation responsibilities.

Recognize particular responses and unanswered conditions without declaring universal harmony or treating private learning as incomplete. Participation is voluntary; required DHS training credit needs an express exception from management, a director or DHS leadership. Native American- and Tribal-specific matters are referred to the appropriate office within ADSA.

sources.title: Council of Europe: Developing intercultural competence through education
sources.note: The examined conceptual sections describe multiple affiliations including family and other groups, personalized meanings, internal variation and intrinsic self-understanding. They inform original example, not legal family definitions or claims about entire populations.

sources.title: Geert Hofstede: The 6D model of national culture
sources.note: The official national-level description distinguishes collectivism from closeness and recognizes within-country variation. The course does not reproduce scores or classify an individual or family with that model.
